48	  ] } },
49	  { type = "paragraph", content = "He looks at you over the top of his glasses." },

55	  ] } },
56	  { type = "paragraph", content = "Behind you your mother moves around the kitchen, humming." },

64	  ] } },
65	  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
66	    { type = "paragraph", content = "He turns back to his reading." },
67	  ] } },
68	  { type = "paragraph", content = "He finishes his coffee." },

# =============================================================================
# Billable Hours — 5 · the people hubs (portraits)
# Each hub: repeatable, `npc` on the trigger (the face and the presence gate,
# engine.md §42), gated on the meeting flag (F5), a leak that shows his want (A13).
# =============================================================================

# ── Martin at breakfast — the leak, and his want +1 a day (capped at 14 in v0.1)
[[canvases]]
id   = "hub_martin_breakfast"
name = "Martin at breakfast"
description = "Martin's hub. The leak by stage; reads her outfit and Ethan's face. Raises his want +1 a day, cap 14."

[canvases.trigger]
location      = "kitchen"
npc           = "npc_martin"
requires_npc  = "npc_martin"
is_repeatable = true
priority      = 6
is_active     = true

[canvases.trigger.conditions]
version = "1.0"
logic   = "AND"
items = [
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "opening_done",    operator = "is_true" },
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "breakfast_today", operator = "is_false" },
]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "table"
name = "Breakfast"
blocks = [
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "time_of_day", start_time = "07:00", end_time = "08:30" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "Martin pours your coffee without asking how you take it. He already knows." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "Martin is at the kitchen table with a whisky and a stack of files. He moves the chair beside him out with his foot." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "He looks at you like he's already decided something." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "martin_stage", operator = "gte", value = 2 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "The jacket, Emma. Friday." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "martin_stage", operator = "eq", value = 1 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Your chair's free on Friday." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Friday, Emma." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "He looks at you over the top of his glasses." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "worn_corruption", operator = "gte", value = 2 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "His eyes go down your tight blouse and stay there long enough that your mother clears her throat at the stove." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "His eyes stay on you a beat too long, and then he turns the page." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Behind you your mother moves around the kitchen, humming." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "ethan_saw_front", operator = "is_true" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "Ethan is staring at his plate like it's a contract." },
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Something wrong with your eggs, Ethan?" },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "He reaches past you for the milk." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "theo_hour_paid", operator = "is_true" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Crisp notes in your envelope this week. Resourceful. I won't ask where from. Not yet." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "He turns back to his reading." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "He finishes his coffee." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "npc", npc_id = "npc_martin", trait_key = "martin_want", operator = "gte", value = 10 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "His hand rests on the back of your chair, and then on your shoulder, and stays there while he reads. He doesn't bother hiding it from the room any more." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "paragraph", content = "His arm brushes yours and he doesn't apologise." },
  ] } },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "choices"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "Sit with him."
targetType = "location"
locationId = "kitchen"
time_progression_minutes = 15
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "breakfast_today", op = "set" } ]
effects = [ { targetType = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin", trait = "martin_want", op = "add", value = 1, cap = 14 } ]

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "Say you're busy and go."
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "hub_martin_breakfast.busy"
show_when_locked = true
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "breakfast_today", op = "set" } ]
effects = [ { targetType = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin", trait = "martin_power", op = "add", value = 1, clamp = true } ]
conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "npc", npc_id = "npc_martin", trait_key = "martin_power", operator = "lt", value = 10 } ] }

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "busy"
name = "Busy"
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "You say you're late and grab your bag. He lets you go without looking up." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Friday, Emma. You won't be busy on Friday." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Go."

[canvases.nodes.exit_block.config]
destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "kitchen"
time_progression_minutes = 5

# ── Diane in the evening ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[canvases]]
id   = "hub_diane_home"
name = "Your mother"
description = "Diane's hub at home. Worried; reads office talk and whether Fridays are 'sweet'."

[canvases.trigger]
location      = "kitchen"
npc           = "npc_diane"
requires_npc  = "npc_diane"
is_repeatable = true
priority      = 6
is_active     = true

[canvases.trigger.conditions]
version = "1.0"
logic   = "AND"
items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "opening_done", operator = "is_true" } ]

id   = "talk"
name = "Your mother"
blocks = [
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "office_talk", operator = "gte", value = 3 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "People at the firm talk, sweetheart. Don't give them anything to talk about. Martin's name is on that door." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "diane_blessed_fridays", operator = "is_true" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "I love that you and Martin have your Fridays now. It means a lot to him. It means a lot to me." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "Are you eating properly? You look tired. Is Callahan being fair to you?" },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She pats the chair next to hers at the table." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "martin_stage", operator = "gte", value = 2 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "You and Martin were up so late on Friday. He came to bed humming. I haven't seen him like that in years." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "The TV on the counter murmurs." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "parents_bed_used", operator = "is_true" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "Martin says I've started making his side of the bed too neatly. I haven't touched it." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She squeezes your hand." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "review_passed", operator = "is_false" }, { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "review_failed", operator = "is_false" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "Week twelve, sweetheart. I've told everyone you'll be kept on. Don't let me down." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "review_failed", operator = "is_true" }, { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "review_passed", operator = "is_false" } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "Probation. I told everyone it was a formality, sweetheart. Make it one." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "Kept on. I told everyone you would be. Now go and get that contract signed." },
  ] } },
]

type = "choices"

targetType = "location"

content.content:
## 37. FOUR condition evaluators, and they do not agree by default

The real architecture is below, and it is the load-bearing fact:

| evaluator | backs | `ne` |
|---|---|---|
| `compare()` — `v2.py:4751` | canvas / node / choice `conditions` | **yes**, since v2 shipped |
| `setup.describeUnmetConditions` — `v2.py:4568`, trait switch `:4591`, phrases `:4602` | the *why is this locked* text on a blocked choice | **yes** |
| `setup.checkSingleCondition` — `v2.py:8736`, trait branch `:8753`, `ne` at `:8775` | hints, quest-card *goal* bullets, `_findFlagSetterCanvas`, ten-plus call sites | **yes** |
| `setup.checkQuestsCondition` — `v2.py:17623` | `[[quest_cards]]` `when` and `goals` | **no, deliberately** |

`compare` is reached first from the trait branch at `v2.py:4842`.

**Anything added to one has to be checked against the other three.** That is the rule this section
exists for; `ne` is just the case that exposed it.

### The four sets, counted 2026-08-29 — and they still do not agree

On a **trait** condition:

| evaluator | operators on a trait |
|---|---|
| `compare()` | `eq` `ne` `gt` `gte` `lt` `lte` `in` `not_in` `contains` `not_contains` `exists` `not_exists` — **12** |
| `describeUnmetConditions` | `eq` `ne` `gt` `gte` `lt` `lte` — **6** |
| `checkSingleCondition` | `eq` `ne` `gt` `gte` `lt` `lte` — **6** |
| `checkQuestsCondition` | `eq` `gt` `gte` `lt` `lte` — **5** |

⚠️ **`ne` is fixed and six operators are not.** `in`, `not_in`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `exists`
and `not_exists` pass `compare()`, so a canvas gate using one **works** — and every other reader
falls through to `return false`. The same condition item is therefore true on the door and false in
the *why is this locked* line, in every hint, and in `_findFlagSetterCanvas`. This is the exact
shape `ne` had before 2026-08-24, still live, times six.

**Not fixed here.** (Type-specific operators — `is_true`, `is_false`,
`is_present`, `equipped`, `owned`, `is_active` and their negations — are their own branches and are
not part of this comparison.) Recorded so the next person adding an operator counts real usage before
the code, and so a game that reaches for `contains` is recognised as the first real demand rather
than as a mystery.

⚠️ **`setup.describeUnmetConditions` is the fourth evaluator**, with its own operator chain and
phrase table. The comment beside `checkSingleCondition`'s `ne` line (`v2.py:8769`) still says "THE
SECOND EVALUATOR": read this table, not that comment, before adding an operator.

### What was actually broken, and what was not

## 39. `time_of_day` — the hour window, and the only predicate that is a window rather than a latch

```toml
{ type = "time_of_day", start_time = "22:00", end_time = "06:00" }   # overnight, wraps midnight
{ type = "time_of_day", start_time = "11:00", end_time = "20:00" }   # ordinary daytime window
{ type = "time_of_day", start_time = "18:00" }                        # no end ⇒ exactly one hour
```

The runtime branch is at `v2.py:4983`; its lock text at `:9096`. `HH:MM`,
24-hour, **end exclusive** — `11:00`–`20:00` is false at 20:00 exactly.

**It delegates.** The branch is four lines and calls `setup.isCurrentTimeSlot`
(`v2.py:4501`) — the same function NPC and location schedules have used since the schedule
primitive shipped. It does not parse hours of its own, so **the overnight wrap has exactly one
implementation** and there is no second copy to drift from the first. That wrap is the trap here: a
hand-rolled `current >= start && current < end` passes every daytime case and fails every window
that crosses midnight, silently.

**Why it exists.** Measured across 27 shipped sandboxes
(`~/Documents/Phone_System_Study_20260829/`), gating content on an hour window is the field's
**second most common mechanism — 20 of 27 games** — behind only a meter gate at 22, and it was the
one item in that list this engine could not express. Locations and NPCs reached the clock through
their `[[schedules]]` rows; a canvas trigger and a phone conversation had no route to it at all, so
"only in the evening" had to be faked by setting a flag from something that does touch the clock.
`the-phone.md` P4.

⚠️ **It is a window, not a latch, and that distinction is the whole reason to prefer it over a
flag.** The predicate is re-evaluated on every read, so it is true only while the clock is inside
the range. **A conversation's delivery, however, still latches** —
`ps.triggered_conversations[conv.id]` (`v2.py:2556`) is written the first time the trigger passes
and never re-read. (A repeatable chat re-arms after it is answered: §51.) So on a phone conversation this predicate means *"deliver this the first time she
is awake at 2am"*, not *"this thread only exists at 2am"*. On a canvas trigger, which is evaluated
fresh, it means the second. **Know which surface you are on.**

**The day of the week is its own predicate** (`weekday`, §52); this one does not take a
`weekdays` list.

⚠️ **Unlike every `worn_*` predicate it carries no `_enabled` guard**, and must not grow one — the
clock is initialised in every build (`time_state` in `$game_state`), including builds with no
schedules, no phone and no clothing.

**Verified live in a built game, not just read.** Ten cases through a real browser against
a built game rebuilt with an overnight condition on a phone conversation: 23:00 and 02:00 inside
`22:00`–`06:00` both true; 21:59, 06:00 and 12:00 false; an ordinary `11:00`–`20:00` window true at
13:00 and false at 20:00 and 10:59; a bare `18:00` true at 18:30 and false at 19:30. Lock text
rendered as `Required: Only between 22:00 and 06:00`. Tests:
`apps/game_generation/tests/test_time_of_day.py`, 11 of 11.

---

## 40. The save-migration seam — what a new release does to an old save

`:: Start` runs once, when a playthrough begins. **SugarCube never re-runs it on load.** So every
default a new release writes there — a flag, a meter, an NPC, a whole system — is `undefined` in
every save that predates it, and the first read throws. The seam that repairs this is the engine's,
not the author's, and knowing its exact reach is the difference between a safe release and a
soft-lock. The authoring rules that follow from it are `references/the-returning-player.md`.

**The skeleton is one object.** `$player` and `$game_state` are serialized into `:: Start` from the
## 52. The day of the week and hours since a flag — `weekday`, `hours_since_flag`

**2026-10-01, opt-in by use.** Two condition types, in every evaluator: the canvas evaluator
(weekday branch at `v2.py:4904`), the lock text, the hint readers, the requirement label, the next-
activity hint (`v2.py:8656`), and quest cards in their own flat shape (`v2.py:17641`).

```toml
{ type = "weekday", weekdays = [5, 6] }        # 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, the schedule rows' index
{ type = "hours_since_flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "met_dan", operator = "gte", value = 3 }

# quest card goal shapes (label required on a goal)
{ weekday = [5], label = "Wait for Saturday" }
{ hours_since_flag = "met_dan", op = "gte", value = 3, label = "Let three hours pass" }
```

- Every flag write stores `set_minute` (day × 1440 + the minute of the day) beside `set_day`:
  `applyFlagEffect`, the closed flag a final no sets (§49) and the cheat restore. `setup.hoursSinceFlag`
  (`v2.py:4708`) fails closed on an unset flag or one with no meta, as `days_since_flag` does.
- **Old saves:** `$flags_meta` is outside the backfill. A flag with `set_day` only reads as set at
  the start of that day (`setup.flagSetMinute`, `v2.py:4684`).
- Import: both are rows in `CONDITION_SCHEMA` (`template_import.py:1663`); `weekday` needs at least
  one day, 0–6, and takes no `operator`. Quest-card shapes: `template_import.py:7244`.
### 32.1 There is no absolute-time advance

```
grep -E 'target_hour|advance_to|until_time|time_target' v2.py     0 hits
```

*(`setTime` matches in this file, but all eight hits are `setTimeout` — a DOM timer for a
notification fade or a deferred `Engine.play`, not a clock setter. Grep for the word, not the
prefix.)*

`window.advanceTime(minutes)` (`v2.py:6559`) adds minutes to `time_state.current_minute`, rolls the
hour past 60 and the day past 24, expires temporary modifiers, and repaints the sidebar. That is the
whole time API. **Nothing in this engine can send the clock to a named hour**, so a label or a beat
promising one ("work till one", "back by six") is a promise the engine cannot keep.

`window.waitTime(minutes)` (`v2.py:6600`) is the sidebar wait buttons' entry point — the same
advance, plus `setup.commitMoment()`, because a wait navigates nowhere and would otherwise live only
in the active moment.

An exit that declares no `time_progression_minutes` still costs **3 minutes**
(`v2.py:15850`, `config.get('default_time_progression', 3)`; the exception fallback at `:16048` emits
the same `advanceTime(3)`). A four-node opening has therefore drifted 9 minutes before the first real
choice.

There is no `@time` token either — `_resolve_at_references` (`v2.py:16695`) resolves `@player` and
`@<npc>` and returns everything else untouched. The clock can be *shown* (`<<timeDisplay>>` at the
top of `StoryCaption`, `v2.py:18529`/`:18546`, rendering `<<timeFormatted>>` at `v2.py:19054`) but it
cannot be *printed into prose* by any authored token.

### 32.2 Travel time is tagged on the card; activity time is tagged nowhere

|---|---|---|

a built game rebuilt with an overnight condition on a phone conversation: 23:00 and 02:00 inside
`22:00`–`06:00` both true; 21:59, 06:00 and 12:00 false; an ordinary `11:00`–`20:00` window true at
13:00 and false at 20:00 and 10:59; a bare `18:00` true at 18:30 and false at 19:30. Lock text

## 40. The save-migration seam — what a new release does to an old save

`:: Start` runs once, when a playthrough begins. **SugarCube never re-runs it on load.** So every
default a new release writes there — a flag, a meter, an NPC, a whole system — is `undefined` in
every save that predates it, and the first read throws. The seam that repairs this is the engine's,
not the author's, and knowing its exact reach is the difference between a safe release and a
soft-lock. The authoring rules that follow from it are `references/the-returning-player.md`.

## 52. The day of the week and hours since a flag — `weekday`, `hours_since_flag`

**2026-10-01, opt-in by use.** Two condition types, in every evaluator: the canvas evaluator
(weekday branch at `v2.py:4904`), the lock text, the hint readers, the requirement label, the next-
activity hint (`v2.py:8656`), and quest cards in their own flat shape (`v2.py:17641`).

```toml
{ type = "weekday", weekdays = [5, 6] }        # 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, the schedule rows' index
{ type = "hours_since_flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "met_dan", operator = "gte", value = 3 }

# quest card goal shapes (label required on a goal)
{ weekday = [5], label = "Wait for Saturday" }
{ hours_since_flag = "met_dan", op = "gte", value = 3, label = "Let three hours pass" }
```

- Every flag write stores `set_minute` (day × 1440 + the minute of the day) beside `set_day`:
  `applyFlagEffect`, the closed flag a final no sets (§49) and the cheat restore. `setup.hoursSinceFlag`
  (`v2.py:4708`) fails closed on an unset flag or one with no meta, as `days_since_flag` does.
- **Old saves:** `$flags_meta` is outside the backfill. A flag with `set_day` only reads as set at
  the start of that day (`setup.flagSetMinute`, `v2.py:4684`).
- Import: both are rows in `CONDITION_SCHEMA` (`template_import.py:1663`); `weekday` needs at least
  one day, 0–6, and takes no `operator`. Quest-card shapes: `template_import.py:7244`.
### 32.1 There is no absolute-time advance

```
grep -E 'target_hour|advance_to|until_time|time_target' v2.py     0 hits
```

*(`setTime` matches in this file, but all eight hits are `setTimeout` — a DOM timer for a
notification fade or a deferred `Engine.play`, not a clock setter. Grep for the word, not the
prefix.)*

`window.advanceTime(minutes)` (`v2.py:6559`) adds minutes to `time_state.current_minute`, rolls the
hour past 60 and the day past 24, expires temporary modifiers, and repaints the sidebar. That is the
whole time API. **Nothing in this engine can send the clock to a named hour**, so a label or a beat
promising one ("work till one", "back by six") is a promise the engine cannot keep.

`window.waitTime(minutes)` (`v2.py:6600`) is the sidebar wait buttons' entry point — the same
advance, plus `setup.commitMoment()`, because a wait navigates nowhere and would otherwise live only
in the active moment.

An exit that declares no `time_progression_minutes` still costs **3 minutes**
(`v2.py:15850`, `config.get('default_time_progression', 3)`; the exception fallback at `:16048` emits
the same `advanceTime(3)`). A four-node opening has therefore drifted 9 minutes before the first real
choice.

There is no `@time` token either — `_resolve_at_references` (`v2.py:16695`) resolves `@player` and
`@<npc>` and returns everything else untouched. The clock can be *shown* (`<<timeDisplay>>` at the
top of `StoryCaption`, `v2.py:18529`/`:18546`, rendering `<<timeFormatted>>` at `v2.py:19054`) but it
cannot be *printed into prose* by any authored token.
